Modify or Extend Existing RTL.medium: For AES-128 to AES-256 upgrades, first align key interface and schedule dimensions together (256-bit i_key, 14 rounds, 60-word expansion); an immediate cocotb out-of-range assignment on i_key is a strong sign the design still has 128-bit assumptions.
Modify or Extend Existing RTL.hard:
If cocotb fails with out-of-range assignment on i_key, treat it as a hard signal that AES-128 key-width assumptions still exist in the staged RTL.
For AES-256 upgrades, change key/input and schedule dimensions together (NBW_KEY=256, expanded key=1920, key-expansion depth=14, decrypt flow through final round index 15).
When decrypt uses 128-bit round keys from a 256-bit schedule, index expanded key with a 128-bit stride (NBW_STEP=NBW_KEY/2) and reverse round order from the last round key.

Integrate multiple modules into a top mo.medium:
If first failure says root/top module missing, check staged RTL for empty or misnamed top file before deeper debugging.
For polyphase decimator integration, map branch samples as shift_window[phase + tap*M] so each branch sees stride-M history.
When submodules register inputs on clk edges, assert branch start one cycle after the M-th sample load to avoid capturing pre-shift data.
Preserve expected hierarchy names in generate blocks/instances (e.g., poly_branches[*].u_poly_filter) when tests use hierarchical coefficient preload. Use timescale at top of rtl code to prevent the cocotb clock period issues
For Icarus/SystemVerilog integration, avoid passing unpacked array slices directly to submodule ports; use per-instance local unpacked arrays in the generate block and wire elements explicitly.
If local eval fails before simulation, verify harness `.env` exists and includes `VERILOG_SOURCES`, `TOPLEVEL`, and `MODULE` for the actual staged RTL files.
For polyphase decimator integration, map branch samples with stride-M indexing (`shift_window[phase + tap*M]`) so each branch sees the correct history.
When upstream storage and branch filters are both edge-triggered, start branch filtering one cycle after the M-th sample load to avoid capturing pre-shift data.
Integrate multiple modules into a top mo.hard:
When harness compile fails with missing top module/file, implement the expected top-level RTL first before deeper debugging.
For wrapper integration around existing crypto blocks, gate all control strobes (`i_start`, key/mode/IV updates, counter reset) to only the selected submodule to keep inactive-path state unchanged.
For byte-replacement padding on fixed 128-bit input blocks, apply padding over LSB bytes only and keep `i_padding_bytes==0` as passthrough behavior.

Debug/fix buggy RTL.medium:
For AES-128 decrypt bugs, validate round ordering first: initial AddRoundKey with the last round key, then 9 inverse rounds, then final round without InvMixColumns.
If key expansion is generated recursively in one combinational pass, derive each next word block from the immediately previous generated key (not from stale packed-expanded storage indices).
When key update and decrypt share one start pulse, latch ciphertext and gate decryption until expanded keys are ready so `o_done` only asserts for completed decrypt output.
